newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola urged to punish killers of journalists.
newsitem.headline: Angola urged to punish killers of journalists.

text.p: Angola has failed to catch the killers of two journalists or to protect press freedom, human rights groups charged on Friday.
"(We) denounce the fact that the killers of journalists in Angola go unpunished, and we condemn the state of press freedom in this country," the groups said.
"To this day, the investigations begun by Angolan authorities into these two cases have reached no conclusion."
In a letter to Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, they said Ricardo de Mello, 38, director of Angola's first independent newspaper, Imparcial Fax, was shot twice on January 18, 1995.

His newspaper had been the target of constant harassment since it started up a year previously and de Mello had received numerous death threats by telephone, the letter from Human Rights Watch Africa and Reporters sans Frontieres said.

At the end of October last year, television journalist Antonio Casimiro was killed in his home by unknown attackers in Cabinda. According to the bishop of Cabinda, the murder was carried out by five policemen led by a civilian, they said.
Casimiro had also been threatened before his death.

The groups charged that the two unpunished killings, plus various death threats and acts of vandalism and intimidation directed against other journalists, had created a "culture of impunity" which seriously limited press freedom in Angola.
"Censorship and self-censorship are omnipresent in publications," the letter charged.

"(We) ask you to inform us about the actual state of investigations into the deaths of Ricardo de Mello and Antonio Casimiro. We ask you to use all your influence to see that they are completed as quickly as possible and perpetrators of these crimes sent to trial."
